page: Amazon Web Services m8i.32xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. The instance is built on the x86_64 architecture using Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors running up to 3.9 GHz. It offers 128 dedicated vCPUs spanning 64 physical cores with 2 threads per core, backed by an expansive 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It is paired with 512.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory (7 GHz), retaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include dedicated instruction sets for advanced acceleration, such as AMX, AVX-512, and AES-NI.

The hardware configuration omits local disk storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for persistent data. It includes a robust 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, though complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included. There are no discrete GPUs bundled with this instance type, focusing its resource profile entirely on central processing capacity and dense system memory.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional parallel execution across the board. Multi-core performance metrics, including stress-ng multi-core (138,379.26), Geekbench multi-core (22,594.0), and PassMark CPU score (122,843.33), consistently reach top-tier status. Single-core performance falls in the moderate to strong range, demonstrating an architectural emphasis on wide multithreading over single-thread peak throughput. Memory bandwidth achieves top-tier results in cached small blocks (10,241.33 GB/sec) and uncached large blocks (392.26 GB/sec read), facilitating intense data manipulation. Real-world workload indicators also place static web serving throughput (203.39 GB/sec) and Redis SET operations (212.78 million ops/sec) in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8i.32xlarge consolidates high-density multithreaded compute and 512 GB of DDR5 memory into a single server, reducing operational fragmentation for large horizontal systems. It is particularly effective for heavy database operations, large-scale software compilation, CPU-based LLM inference, caching layers, and high-throughput web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m8i.32xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro instance powered by 128 dedicated vCPUs (64 physical cores) from Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors clocked at 3.9 GHz, coupled with 512.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz. Based on x86_64 architecture with AMX and AVX-512 acceleration, the instance provides 50 Gbps baseline networking, no local storage, and zero GPUs. Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded processing, reflected in high PassMark and Geekbench multi-core scores, alongside superior memory bandwidth reaching 392.26 GB/sec on uncached reads. Real-world performance shows exceptional results in Redis operations (212.78 million ops/sec) and static web serving (203.39 GB/sec). With its balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio and extensive core count, the instance is well suited for enterprise databases, massive software compilation, Redis clusters, and mid-to-large CPU-based LLM inference.
